solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wrinkled floor covering in front of huge entrance to edifice

indicators.note: the floor covering is placed ahead of what follows in the answer

parts.note: a rug is a small carpet laid on a floor
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: the entrance of a word is its opening letter, here of edifice

explanation.surface: Someone notices a crumpled rug lying before the grand doorway of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugose is a botanical and anatomical term for a surface covered in creases or ridges.

clue.text: Curtail support, internal scheme being inadequate

indicators.note: the shortened scheme goes inside the support

parts.note: a rest is something that supports, like an armrest

indicators.note: the scheme falls short, missing its last letter

parts.note: a trick is a crafty scheme

explanation.surface: Cutting back funding because the in-house plan is not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being inadequate' means the scheme falls one letter short (dropping K); 'internal' places the shortened scheme inside the support.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrict is to limit or confine, which is to curtail.

clue.text: Social awkwardness of Erica, huge, dishevelled

indicators.note: the letters are left untidy and disordered, like messy hair

explanation.surface: A large, scruffy woman named Erica displays social clumsiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaucherie, from French 'left-handed', is tactless or clumsy behaviour.

clue.text: Very good house useless in part of London

parts.note: 'just so' or simply 'so' answers 'very good', agreeing that something is fine

indicators.note: the house loses the letters spelling use, so it is without use

parts.note: the word house is used as written before the cut

explanation.surface: A fine house that serves no purpose in a district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'useless' is read as 'use-less': take USE out of HOUSE to leave HO.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a district of London's West End known for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Supporting two girls (one named) seen to be extravagant

parts.note: to be pro something is to be in favour of it
Di, short for Diana, is the named girl and gal is an informal word for any girl

explanation.surface: A man backing two young women at once is seen to be spending lavishly.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket tells you only one of the girls is a name: DI, then GAL, a general word for a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Prodigal describes someone wastefully lavish with money, as in the parable's son.

clue.text: When madam does this it makes no difference

definitions.text: When madam does this it makes no difference

parts.words: When madam does this it makes no difference
parts.note: madam reads the same backwards, so turning it round changes nothing

explanation.surface: A remark that a lady's actions change nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Madam is a palindrome, so when it goes back the other way it is unchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back the way one came, or be read backwards, is what a palindrome does with no effect.

clue.text: Record on, sure thing to upset

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
a cert is a certainty, a racing term for a sure winner

explanation.surface: Putting a record on is a guaranteed way to annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: CERT is British slang for a dead certainty, especially a horse sure to win.
explanation.definitionFit: To disconcert is to unsettle or fluster someone.

clue.text: Good to have wet weather? It may stop this being harvested

definitions.text: It may stop this being harvested

parts.note: rain is wet weather

explanation.surface: A farmer wonders if rain is welcome, since it may halt the harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'it' as the rain just given and 'this' as the answer: rain can stop a cereal crop being gathered.
explanation.definitionFit: Wheat and barley are cut in dry weather; a downpour can stop that cereal crop being gathered in.

clue.text: Extra line, say, written before Cheerio

indicators.note: the line word is put ahead of the farewell

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means here
bye is an informal goodbye, like cheerio

explanation.surface: A note on adding an extra line before signing off.
explanation.walkthrough: A leg bye is a cricket run scored after the ball glances off the batsman's body; it counts as an extra, not to the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a leg bye is one of the extras, runs not credited to any batsman.

clue.text: Club joined by the female swimmer?

indicators.note: the club word is followed by the female

parts.note: a bat is a club for hitting a ball
her is the female pronoun

explanation.surface: A sports club is joined by a woman who swims?
explanation.definitionFit: A bather is someone who swims in the sea or a pool.

clue.text: Direction taken by Caesar in retreat

definitions.text: Direction taken by Caesar in retreat

parts.words: Direction taken by Caesar in retreat
parts.note: 'Direction' defines; 'taken by Caesar' picks the two middle letters E and S of the name, and 'in retreat' turns them, giving the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A history question about which way the Roman general went when he pulled back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken by' lifts E and S from inside 'Caesar' and 'in retreat' reverses them; the result is the standard abbreviation for this compass point, which the grid spells out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: This compass bearing lies midway between two cardinal points, south and east, and its usual short form is two letters.

clue.text: Serious language may limit it

indicators.note: the two words act as bounds holding the answer between them, its letters spanning the end of one and start of the other

explanation.surface: A remark that formal speech tends to restrict casual expressions.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the last of 'Serious' into the start of 'language', and the whole clue also describes how formal speech keeps informal words in check.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal, serious speech tends to exclude colloquial vocabulary, so it restricts this informal register.

clue.text: Some worker hurrying around industrial region

indicators.note: the run picked out is turned back to front
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: A labourer rushing about in a manufacturing district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks RHUR from 'worker hurrying'; 'around' turns it to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ruhr valley in western Germany is famous for coal mining and heavy industry.

clue.text: Somerset town having refusal, one way and another, to offer wine

parts.note: Chard is a market town in Somerset, a county in south-west England

indicators.note: the refusal is read in one direction, backwards, here

parts.note: no is a refusal
another word for a refusal, nay, follows

explanation.surface: A West Country town offers wine after saying no twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one way' reverses NO to ON; 'and another' gives a second refusal, NAY, in a different form.
explanation.definitionFit: Chardonnay is a white grape variety and the dry white wine made from it.

clue.text: They travel around in the trains — not hard, tipsy

indicators.note: the remaining letters lurch drunkenly into a new order
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard, and it is taken away

explanation.surface: Travellers on trains who are, if not drunk, at least a little merry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not hard' removes H from IN THE TRAINS, and 'tipsy' rearranges INTETRAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Itinerants are people who move from place to place, without fixed home.

clue.text: Custodian of gold meeting minister in church briefly

indicators.note: the minister's word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a curate is an assistant clergyman in a parish
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone guarding treasure meets a clergyman in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks CURATE to CURAT, which is followed by OR.
explanation.definitionFit: A curator is the keeper in charge of a museum or gallery collection.

clue.text: Island showing cold nature following sun

indicators.note: the cold piece comes after the sun's letter

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for sun, as in Sunday
acting with a cold nature is behaving icily

explanation.surface: An island displays a chilly character despite coming after the sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicily is the large Mediterranean island off the toe of Italy.

clue.text: Possibly send things yet to be sorted out?

definitions.text: things yet to be sorted out

parts.note: read the pieces as wordplay: loose is an anagram signal and ends shuffled gives the clue's send

explanation.surface: Maybe dispatch the items still awaiting attention?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer, as wordplay, tells you to loosen ENDS, which makes SEND, and 'Possibly' flags that ENDS is just one rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose ends are details or tasks still left unfinished.

clue.text: Sour gent upset by female nationalist

indicators.note: the letters are upset, overturned into a different order

explanation.surface: A grumpy man is put out by a woman campaigning for her nation.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicola Sturgeon led the Scottish National Party and was Scotland's First Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicola Sturgeon is the former SNP leader and First Minister of Scotland.

clue.text: Note about what cheese-maker needs

indicators.note: the note's word is turned round

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: A remark on the ingredients a cheese-maker requires.
explanation.walkthrough: A TENNER is a £10 note in British slang; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is the curdling agent, traditionally from calves' stomachs, used to set milk into cheese.

clue.text: Adolescent is rebellious free agent, putting father off

indicators.note: the remaining letters refuse their order and rebel into a new one
the father's letters are put off, removed

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: A defiant youngster declares independence, shrugging off his dad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting ... off' removes FR from FREE AGENT; 'rebellious' rearranges EEAGENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenage describes someone in their teens, an adolescent.

clue.text: To subcontract is weird, a thousand being drafted in

indicators.note: the thousand is brought into the middle of the weird phrase

parts.note: far out is slang for strange or unconventional
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Handing work to contractors is odd when a thousand people are conscripted.
explanation.definitionFit: To farm out work is to pass it to outside contractors rather than do it in-house.

clue.text: Draw attention to a Parisian imprisoned in apartment

indicators.note: the French word is shut inside the apartment

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
un is French for a

explanation.surface: A Parisian locked in a flat tries to draw notice to his plight.
explanation.definitionFit: To flaunt something is to show it off ostentatiously.

clue.text: Journalist maybe travelled north to pen the article?

indicators.note: the travelling word encloses the article like a pen holding sheep
in a down answer going north is reading upwards, so backwards

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback or by vehicle
it stands for the thing in question, the article just mentioned

explanation.surface: A reporter perhaps headed north to write the piece?
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light 'north' means read upwards, giving EDOR; 'to pen' means to enclose, like a sheep pen.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is one kind of journalist, the one who runs a paper or section.

clue.text: Exotic dish cooked by baker, horribly black

parts.note: food that is done has been cooked through

indicators.note: the letters are messed up horribly into a new order

parts.note: B is the pencil-grading abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: A baker has burnt something foreign to a dreadful blackness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horribly' rearranges the baker's letters plus B into RKEBAB; 'cooked' looks like the anagram signal but supplies its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: This Turkish dish of spit-roasted sliced meat in bread is a foreign takeaway staple.

clue.text: State speed with which goddess becomes manifest

parts.note: NY is the abbreviation for New York State
mph, miles per hour, measures speed

explanation.surface: A deity materialises in an American state at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth nymphs are minor female deities of rivers, woods and hills.

clue.text: Part of crop, early fruit

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a harvest comes in ahead of the season, some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet orchard fruit of the apple family.

clue.text: Instrument, one deceptive to the audience

indicators.note: what the listeners hear is a word that sounds alike

parts.note: a liar is someone who deceives

explanation.surface: A musician plays a stringed instrument to deceive the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is an ancient harp-like stringed instrument.

clue.text: As an Athenian, this writer's in the fashion

indicators.note: the writer's piece sits inside the fashion word

parts.note: the ton is an old word for high fashion or society
this writer is the setter, and 'this writer is' shortens to I'm

explanation.surface: A writer claims to be fashionable, as an Athenian would be.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's misanthrope in Timon of Athens is the best-known Athenian of that name.

clue.text: Anyone can get upset, showing irritation

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are upset, knocked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Anybody can become cross, displaying vexation.
explanation.definitionFit: Annoyance is the feeling of being irked or vexed.

clue.text: She hears about new arrangements for old things

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are moved about into another order

explanation.surface: A woman learns of fresh plans for familiar items.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehashes are reworkings of old material presented as if new.

clue.text: Boy joining theatre about to be seen as an individual

indicators.note: the boy is attached to the theatre piece
the theatre word is turned round

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A lad joining a theatre company is about to become noticed in his own right.
explanation.walkthrough: Rep is short for repertory theatre, a company performing a changing programme; 'about' turns it to PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A person is a single human being, one individual.
